section: Sky Lab: Observe — Eyepiece field lab
changes: True angular scale replaces target enlargement and shrinking-to-fit; a circular SVG clip crops the field
Aperture and telescope focal length are independent native controls
Quick eyepiece comparisons keep magnification controls beside the field
Readable captions, field width, exit pupil, focal ratio and a live status stay outside the circular image
Gaussian seeing blur uses the same angular scale as the target
Bortle qualitatively changes sky brightness and sketch contrast without making detection claims
Measured telescope dimensions and included eyepieces provide real instrument presets
The Whirlpool Galaxy and Double Cluster have distinct schematic views

equations.magnification: telescope focal length / eyepiece focal length
equations.seeing: Gaussian sigma = seeing FWHM / field width in arcsec × field diameter in pixels / 2.355

data.scope: Targets use fixed example angular extents. Shapes, colors, phases and star positions are illustrative. Apparent field defaults to 60 degrees as a teaching choice, and instrument presets preserve this user setting. Field-stop measurements and eyepiece distortion are omitted. Seeing is a Gaussian approximation, independent of the Dawes double-star criterion. Bortle contrast is qualitative. Diffraction, optical aberrations and eye response are omitted; the sketch does not predict detectability tonight.

checks: Independent controls, keyboard steps, preserved focus and saved state
Instrument presets preserve apparent field and sky settings
Minimum 44px touch controls and no horizontal overflow
No runtime errors or unhandled promise rejections in tested scenarios
